data.title: RCS - MonEuroSmllCosTst - MESCT 20 years investing in Europe's hidden gems
data.description:
RNS Number : 8228U Montanaro European Smaller C.TstPLC 15 September 2026  

Montanaro European Smaller Companies Trust celebrates 20 years of investing in Europe's hidden gems

·      Annualised NAV total return of 10.2%, net of fees, compared with 8.5% for its benchmark

·      Portfolio of around 50 holding selected by one of the largest, most experienced specialist investment teams focused on European SmallCap

·      Long-term strategy focused on finding tomorrow's winners at today's prices

Montanaro European Smaller Companies Trust (MESCT) is proud to be celebrating 20 years under the management of Montanaro Asset Management, marking two decades of investing in quoted smaller companies across Continental Europe.

Over the past two decades, the Trust has navigated the Global Financial Crisis, the Eurozone sovereign debt crisis, the Covid-19 pandemic, changing interest rates and investor sentiment, and often challenging macroeconomic conditions. Despite this backdrop, it has delivered an annualised NAV total return of 10.2%, net of fees, compared with 8.5% for the MSCI Europe ex-UK SmallCap Index and 6.9% for the FTSE All-Share Index, in each case with dividends reinvested.

The Trust's portfolio of around 50 holdings is built through bottom-up stock selection by one of the largest specialist teams in Europe. The team seeks to find tomorrow's winners at today's prices by identifying profitable, growing businesses with strong market positions and outstanding management teams capable of compounding value over time.

While markets have changed considerably since 2006, MAM's investment philosophy has remained consistent. Its approach combines detailed proprietary research, disciplined stock selection and patient ownership, with the team meeting management teams and visiting companies across Europe.

Gordon Neilly, Chairman of Montanaro European Smaller Companies Trust, said: "Twenty years under MAM's stewardship is an important milestone for the Trust. Over that period, it has delivered an annualised NAV total return of 10.2%, net of fees, while navigating multiple economic and market cycles.

"This enduring partnership reflects our shared conviction that European smaller companies offer compelling opportunities for patient, long-term investors, as well as the dedication of MAM's investment team in identifying and analysing those businesses.

"On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank our shareholders for their continued support and the team at Montanaro for its commitment to the Trust over the past 20 years."

George Cooke, Portfolio Manager of Montanaro European Smaller Companies Trust, said: "For two decades, the Trust has sought to identify some of Europe's highest-quality smaller companies before they become widely recognised. These businesses are often leaders in specialist markets, with strong competitive advantages and the ability to compound earnings over many years.

"European smaller companies remain relatively under-researched and, following a prolonged period out of favour, valuations are attractive. We believe this presents a compelling opportunity for patient, active investors willing to look beyond short-term market noise."

As MESCT enters its third decade under Montanaro's management, it will continue to offer investors a differentiated way to access the long-term growth potential of European smaller companies.

ENDS

Camarco, PR Advisers

Ben Woodford / Elfie Harkell / Annabel Reed

montanaro@camarco.co.uk

Notes to Editors

Montanaro European Smaller Companies Trust is a London-listed investment trust aiming for long-term capital growth by investing in high-quality, small-cap companies listed in Europe, particularly within the EU, Norway, and Switzerland.  Managed by Montanaro Asset Management, MESCT aims to achieve capital growth by investing in small European quoted companies.  It seeks to achieve capital growth in excess of its benchmark, the MSCI Europe SmallCap (ex-UK) Index.

In February 2026, the Association of Investment Companies (AIC) listed MESCT among 68 investment trusts that would have made investors more than £1 million if they had invested the full annual ISA allowance in the same trust each year.  This is a reflection of the proven and consistent long-term performance and track record of the Montanaro European Smaller Companies Trust.

data.title: Prices ease from fresh highs, but LNG supply stays tight
data.description:
Key points:
  • European gas storage is just 68% full, 12 percentage points less than a year ago
  • LNG supply disruptions keep market tight
  • French LNG terminal strike offset by higher wind, solar, Norwegian gas flows

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices eased from near four-year highs on Tuesday morning but remain supported by ongoing disruptions to liquefied natural gas (LNG) supply from the Middle East and Europe's efforts to replenish gas storage.

A strike at a French LNG terminal is expected to have limited impact.

The benchmark Dutch front-month contract at the TTF hub (TFMBMc1) fell €0.70 to €81.87 per megawatt hour (MWh) by 0801 GMT, ICE data showed.

The British front-month contract (NGLNMc1) fell by 1.85 pence to 203.34 pence per therm.

Prices have come off fresh intraday highs seen on Monday but remain close to levels last seen in December 2022, analysts said.

"Middle East concerns and tight global LNG availability at times when storage build is lagging behind keep supporting to the upside," analysts at Mind Energy said in a daily note.

Moves in the JKM-TTF spread, which measures the difference in Asian to European gas prices, suggest that Europe should be pulling in LNG spot cargoes, although it will be difficult for Europe to hit its lower storage target of 75% ahead of winter, they added.

EU gas storage is 68.2% full, 16.2 percentage points below the five-year average, according to data from Gas Infrastructure Europe.

Meanwhile, a 24-hour labour strike in France's power sector on Tuesday is expected to reduce delivery capacity at the Dunkirk LNG terminal by almost half.

However, the effect is likely to be partly absorbed by terminals in the Netherlands and Belgium and by Montoir in France, LSEG analyst Dzmitry Dauhalevich said.

Higher German wind and solar output, Norwegian gas production above 300 million cubic metres (mcm) per day and above-normal temperatures in continental Europe also limited the short-term impact of the strike, a trader said.

Total Norwegian export bookings were at 304.9 mcm per day on Tuesday, the first time they have climbed above 300 mcm/day since late August, according to data from infrastructure operator Gassco.

In the European carbon market, the benchmark contract fell €0.78 to €87.21 per metric ton.

data.title: EQT, Norges team up to bid for Acciona Energia, Expansion reports
data.description:
Swedish private equity firm EQT and Norges Bank Investment Management, the manager of Norway's sovereign wealth fund, are launching a joint bid for Acciona Energia , Spanish newspaper Expansion reported on Tuesday, citing market sources.

The consortium faces competition for the renewable energy company from French private equity firm Ardian, which is 91.1% owned by Acciona , the group controlled by the Entrecanales family, the newspaper added.

  • Acciona Energia's enterprise value, including debt, is about €11.9 billion ($13.73 billion), according to LSEG data.

  • EQT is participating through its infrastructure division and holds around 75% of the consortium, while Norges Bank IM would hold the remaining 25%, Expansion reported.

  • Acciona declined to comment. EQT and Norges did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

  • The sale process has progressed beyond non-binding bids, with Acciona Energia arranging meetings between the most interested candidates and management before bidders confirm their proposed prices in October, according to the report.

  • Spanish conglomerate Acciona would then be expected to select a preferred proposal and enter exclusive talks. Any agreement would be expected to lead to a takeover offer aimed at delisting the company, Expansion said.

  • Ardian is assessing the acquisition through its infrastructure business and has not formed an alliance, although Expansion said the transaction's size would require it to at least seek co-investors.

  • Acciona is working with Citi and Goldman Sachs to assess strategic options for the subsidiary, the newspaper reported.

  • Its Chairman Jose Manuel Entrecanales has previously described a sale of the entire subsidiary as "extremely unlikely", outlining other options including a stake sale.

  • Shares in Acciona Energía were up 3.3% at 0757 GMT, while shares of Acciona were 3.1% higher. EQT shares were down 3.2%.

($1 = 0.8669 euros)

data.title: Malaysia raises October crude palm oil reference price, duty remains at 10%
data.description:
Malaysia has raised its October crude palm oil reference price to a level that maintains the export duty at 10%, a circular on the Malaysian Palm Oil Board website showed on Tuesday.

The world's second-largest palm exporter calculated a reference price of 4,452.66 ringgit ($1,091.34) per metric ton for October.

The September reference price was 4,392.32 ringgit a ton, and incurred a duty of 10%.

The export tax structure starts at 3% for crude palm oil in a 2,250-to-2,400 ringgit-per-ton range. The maximum tax rate is set at 10% when prices exceed 4,050 ringgit a ton.

($1 = 4.0800 ringgit)

data.title: AU SFB Strengthens Leadership With Anil Agarwal, Amol Padhye Appointments
data.description:
Agarwal will lead Commercial & Institutional Banking, while Padhye takes charge of risk management as AU SFB prepares for its next phase of growth and proposed transition to a Universal Bank

AU Small Finance Bank (AU SFB) has appointed Anil Agarwal as Senior Executive Group Head – Commercial & Institutional Banking and Amol Padhye as Chief Risk Officer (CRO), strengthening its leadership structure as it prepares for its next phase of growth and proposed transition to a Universal Bank.

The appointments are aimed at strengthening the bank’s capabilities across commercial and institutional banking as well as enterprise-wide risk management, with a focus on governance, disciplined growth and long-term value creation.

Anil Agarwal To Lead Commercial & Institutional Banking

Agarwal brings nearly three decades of experience across commercial and institutional banking, transaction banking, government business, corporate banking, financial institutions and capital markets.

In his new role, he will provide strategic leadership and integrated oversight across AU SFB’s Commercial & Institutional Banking platform. His mandate will cover Commercial Banking, Wholesale Liabilities, Transaction Banking & Cash Management Services, Financial Institutions & Capital Markets, Government Banking and Sustainability initiatives.

Before joining AU SFB, Agarwal spent more than two decades at Axis Bank, where he held senior leadership roles across Financial Institutions, Government Business, Transaction Banking, Strategic Client Coverage, Corporate Banking and Priority Sector Lending Strategy.

Earlier, he worked with IFCI in Project Finance and Credit.

Agarwal is a rank-holder Chartered Accountant (CA) and Cost & Management Accountant (CMA). His experience spans building and scaling customer franchises across corporate, government and financial institution segments, alongside a focus on governance and disciplined execution.

Amol Padhye Named Chief Risk Officer

Amol Padhye has been appointed Chief Risk Officer, bringing more than 23 years of experience across enterprise risk management, credit risk, market and liquidity risk, model risk management and emerging technology risk governance.

A Chartered Accountant, Padhye joins AU SFB after holding senior leadership positions at HDFC Bank and EY, where he worked on risk transformation, governance and regulatory initiatives across the financial services sector.

At AU SFB, he will lead the bank’s Risk Management function, with a mandate focused on strengthening enterprise-wide risk governance, regulatory readiness and risk management frameworks while supporting the bank’s growth plans.

Commenting on the appointments, Sanjay Agarwal, Founder, MD & CEO, AU Small Finance Bank, says, “At AU SFB, we have always believed that enduring institutions are built on strong leadership, disciplined execution and a long-term commitment to sustainable growth. As we continue to strengthen our capabilities across businesses and governance functions, investing in leadership depth remains a key priority.

Anil has earned a reputation for building and nurturing customer franchises, strategic foresight and balancing growth with institutional resilience, while Amol brings extensive experience in strengthening risk governance and organisational resilience. Together, these appointments reinforce our focus on building a future-ready institution, balancing scale with sustainability, and creating long-term value for our customers, employees and shareholders.”

Anil Agarwal, Senior Executive Group Head – Commercial & Institutional Banking, AU Small Finance Bank, says, “AU SFB has established itself as one of India's most admired financial institutions by combining entrepreneurial agility with strong governance and customer focus.

I am delighted to join AU SFB at this exciting phase of its growth journey and look forward to working closely with the leadership team to further strengthen and scale the Commercial & Institutional Banking franchise, deepen client relationships and deliver differentiated solutions that support businesses across the country. I am confident that AU SFB's distinctive culture, exceptional talent and long-term vision will continue to create enduring value for customers, shareholders and all stakeholders.”

Amol Padhye, Chief Risk Officer, AU Small Finance Bank, says, “AU SFB's success has been built on a strong foundation of prudent risk management, customer trust and responsible growth. I am privileged to assume this role at a time when the banking industry is evolving rapidly amid new opportunities and emerging risks.

My focus will be on further strengthening the Bank's risk culture, leveraging data, technology and analytics to improve decision-making, and ensuring that risk management continues to serve as a strategic enabler of AU SFB's long-term ambitions. Together, we will continue strengthening the Bank's resilience while enabling sustainable and responsible growth.”

The appointments come as AU SFB continues to strengthen its leadership architecture and institutional capabilities. The bank has received in-principle approval from the Reserve Bank of India to transition into a Universal Bank, positioning the latest appointments within its broader efforts to build capabilities for its next phase of expansion.

data.title: Classplus Names Ankit Maheshwari As CFO
data.description:
Maheshwari joins Classplus after leading finance at Zupee, bringing more than 13 years of experience across technology, auto e-commerce, capital strategy and business finance

Classplus has appointed Ankit Maheshwari as Chief Financial Officer (CFO), with the finance executive moving from Zupee, where he served as Head of Finance. Maheshwari brings more than 13 years of experience across technology, entertainment tech and auto e-commerce, with his work spanning fundraising, financial planning, capital strategy, governance, controls and business transformation.

Move From Zupee

Maheshwari joins Classplus after serving as Head of Finance at Zupee. His responsibilities there included supporting the company’s finance function across planning, controls, capital management and business decision-making.

The appointment marks his move into a CFO role after holding senior finance positions across businesses operating in fast-growing technology-led sectors.

At Classplus, his mandate is expected to cover financial controls, business insights, capital allocation and strengthening the role of finance in supporting wider business decisions.

Earlier Role At Cars24

Before Zupee, Maheshwari served as Head of Finance and Vice President at Cars24.

His responsibilities at the company covered investor relations, treasury, financial planning and analysis, business finance, controllership, taxation, risk, governance, supply chain finance and finance transformation.

He was also involved in financial efficiency, unit economics and regulatory compliance while overseeing finance responsibilities across several operational and strategic areas.

Experience Across Finance Functions

Across his career, Maheshwari has worked on project financing, equity and debt fundraising, financial modelling, capital strategy, governance and business transformation.

His experience also includes building finance processes, strengthening controls and supporting businesses through periods of expansion and operational change.

Earlier in his career, he worked with Den Networks and IBM, where he gained experience across financial analysis and operational finance.

New Finance Leadership Role

Maheshwari is a Chartered Accountant and has completed a CFO Programme from IIM Calcutta. He also holds a B.Com degree from Rajasthan University.

His appointment gives Classplus a finance leader with experience across fundraising, treasury, planning, governance and business finance as the company develops its next phase of financial and operational priorities.

data.title: Credit Agricole sees MPS bid for Banco BPM as unappealing, paper says
data.description:
French bank Credit Agricole , the biggest investor in Italian lender Banco BPM , sees an offer by rival Banca Monte dei Paschi (MPS) for BPM as unattractive and doubts it will deliver value for shareholders, daily La Stampa reported on Tuesday.

The bid for Banco BPM is part of a two-pronged defence strategy, which also includes an offer for wealth manager Banca Generali , that MPS CEO Luigi Lovaglio presented in August to fend off a takeover plan by Intesa Sanpaolo .

Credit Agricole owns 29.3% of Banco BPM, and opposition from one of the targets' top investors would be a major hurdle for Lovaglio, who also needs MPS's own shareholders to first approve the plan in a vote on October 29.

Credit Agricole has conveyed its negative view on the proposal in a meeting with Lovaglio a few days ago, La Stampa said. It said that the French bank looked instead at a merger between its Italian unit and Banco BPM.

Credit Agricole has previously said that such a tie-up is its preferred option and had rejected the prospect of a "merger of equals" Banco BPM and MPS had been negotiating.

When those talks collapsed, MPS unveiled its takeover bid for BPM on terms which MPS CEO Lovaglio has said are similar to those the two banks had previously been discussing.

MPS and Credit Agricole declined to comment.

Any BPM-Credit Agricole Italia deal is a long way away, La Stampa said, because terms would have to be agreed first that please other BPM shareholders and reassurances given to Italy's government.

Credit Agricole, for which Italy is the biggest foreign market, has worked to keep good relations with Rome.

The support of the other BPM investors is necessary because Credit Agricole would not be allowed to take part in the shareholder vote on the transaction.

($1 = 0.8669 euros)

data.title: German wholesale prices post fastest rise in over 3 years on energy costs
data.description:
German wholesale prices rose at their fastest rate in more than three years in August, as the conflict in Iran and the Middle East drives up costs for energy products and raw materials in particular, the federal statistics office said on Tuesday.

Wholesale prices - an early indicator of inflation trends - increased by 6.8% in August compared with the same month last year, according to the office.

The last higher monthly reading was February 2023 at 9.5%, said the office.

Compared with the previous month, prices saw a 0.9% rise.

"As in previous months, the price increase registered in August 2026 was largely attributable to the conflict in Iran and the Middle East, which resulted in higher wholesale prices of energy products and raw materials, in particular," it said.

Prices for petroleum products surged by 36.1% on the year, while prices for chemical products rose by 13.6%.

German inflation has been hovering above the European Central Bank's 2% target since the start of the war in Iran in late February, with a latest reading of 2.9% in August.

ECB executive board member Isabel Schnabel called the recent energy price increases "quite concerning" on Monday, and the central bank last week raised interest rates for the second time this year and revised up many of its inflation forecasts.

data.title: Sterling Could Weaken if BOE Dampens Rate-Rise Bets — Market Talk
data.description: Sterling is at risk of falling if the Bank of England remains cautious about raising interest rates, ING's Francesco Pesole says in a note. The BOE is likely to leave rates on hold Thursday and stress there is no evidence price pressures are extending beyond energy prices, he says. BOE Governor Andrew Bailey could also push back against aggressive rate rise expectations. U.K fiscal worries ahead of the October budget and growing pressure on the U.K. government to allow independence referendums in Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland could also weigh on sterling, he says. The euro rises 0.1% to 0.8560 pounds and ING targets an increase to 0.8700 pounds in the coming weeks.(renae.dyer@wsj.com)

data.title: Bitpanda CEO to go to Austria's Erste Group, kicking off leader search at crypto broker
data.description:
The CEO of Bitpanda, a Vienna-based broker specialized in crypto assets, is leaving next year to take a role at Austria's Erste Group , the companies said on Tuesday.

  • Lukas Enzersdorfer-Konrad, the Bitpanda CEO, will join Erste as executive director of group asset management in the first quarter of 2027.

  • Meanwhile, he remains CEO at Bitpanda and will be joined effective immediately by a new co-CEO, Christian Trummer, a Bitpanda co-founder and chief scientist.

  • Bitpanda has started a search for Enzersdorfer-Konrad's successor, looking internally and externally.

  • Erste said the group asset management director job is newly created and will report directly to the bank's CEO.

  • "I was not looking for a new job ... But sometimes life happens differently, and I got an opportunity, which I simply could not refuse," Enzersdorfer-Konrad told Reuters in a brief interview.

  • He has been Bitpanda CEO since August 2025.

  • Trummer told Reuters it made sense for the two to lead as co-CEOs.

  • "I've been helping to build this company from day one. I'm in the office every day. People know me. I'm very well connected with the management team," Trummer said.

data.title: Norway Trade Logs Biggest Surplus Since Early 2023
data.description:
OSLO (dpa-AFX) - Norway's foreign trade surplus expanded significantly in August, driven by robust export growth that outpaced import increases, according to data released Tuesday by Statistics Norway.

The trade surplus climbed to NOK 100.4 billion in August from NOK 59.3 billion in the same month last year. This represented the largest trade surplus since January 2023. In July, the surplus had totaled NOK 88.8 billion.

Exports surged 32.9 percent annually in August, while imports rose 7.3 percent over the same period. Natural gas exports led the growth with an 80.9 percent year-over-year increase. Crude oil exports also demonstrated strong performance, climbing 12.7 percent annually.

Mainland exports increased 12.3 percent annually and 4.8 percent monthly in August. The mainland trade deficit narrowed to NOK 19.9 billion from NOK 22.9 billion in July.

data.title: India's proposals to revamp derivatives settlement could alleviate expiry-day volatility, analysts say
data.description:
By Jayshree P Upadhyay and Vivek Kumar M

The Indian markets regulator's proposed revamp of expiry-day settlement for derivatives could curb volatility and clear a key overhang for the options market, analysts said, easing concerns that have weighed on trading since the launch of the closing auction session (CAS).

The CAS framework was introduced on August 3 for stocks that have futures and options contracts. Under this system, a short auction at the end of the trading day helps determine the closing price of a stock. However, the new process led to sharp swings in derivatives prices on expiry days, prompting the regulator to review it.

In a consultation paper released on Saturday, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) proposed two ways to set expiry-day derivative prices.

Under the first option, the settlement price would be calculated using trades from the last 30 minutes of regular trading as well as the 10-minute closing auction.

The second option would mark a temporary return to the earlier method of using only the last 30 minutes of regular trading. The closing auction would not be used to calculate derivatives settlement prices for at least a year.

"SEBI is clearly trying to make CAS more predictable and reduce the uncertainty it created for derivatives, particularly on expiry days, without reversing CAS itself," analysts at IIFL Capital said in a note on Tuesday.

SEBI has also proposed other changes to make the closing auction smoother. It wants to stop traders from cancelling orders placed more than 1% above or below the reference price, cut the post-auction derivatives trading window to five minutes from 10 minutes, and stop publishing an estimated index closing level during the auction.

Jefferies said that returning to a volume-weighted average price, or VWAP, for derivatives settlement — along with tighter rules on cancelling orders — should help reduce sharp price swings near the close on expiry days.

Brokerages said the proposals could lower the risk of sudden price distortions caused by uncertainty over the final settlement price.

IIFL Capital said a return to VWAP-based settlement could bring back some derivatives trading that moved away after CAS was introduced. However, it said the scale of any recovery is difficult to estimate without detailed trader-level data.

The last date to submit responses to SEBI's consultation paper is October 3, with Jefferies saying it expects changes to be implemented in October or November this year.

data.title: Indonesia's Finance Minister Pick Could Be Tonic Markets Want
data.description:
By Amanda Lee and Fabiana Negrin Ochoa

Indonesia has appointed its third finance minister in under two years. That shouldn't inspire much confidence, but analysts say the experienced technocrat could be an antidote for worries about erratic policymaking.

Suahasil Nazara steps into the role with a solid track record. A seasoned economist, he spent almost seven years as deputy finance minister, including under Sri Mulyani Indrawati, the respected former finance minister whose ouster in late 2025 was one of the catalysts that contributed to Indonesian markets' loss of credibility.

He inherits a challenging position: Keeping the budget deficit below the 3% legal ceiling while balancing expansive social programs such as the government's flagship free-meals program.

External headwinds abound too. Drawn-out fighting in the Middle East is keeping energy prices high, heaping pressure on the oil-sensitive rupiah, threatening to swell Indonesia's import bill and adding fiscal strain.

A sustained rise in oil prices could bring Indonesia's fuel subsidy bill to as much as 1.1% of gross domestic product, necessitating expenditure cuts, OCBC economists Lavanya Venkateswaran and Ahmad A Enver said.

Then there's the crisis of confidence among foreign investors. Indonesia's assets have fallen out of favor this year as ratings companies and index providers flagged issues around transparency and investability.

Still, analysts say Suahasil has a shot at winning back investor and institutional confidence.

The initial market reaction to President Prabowo Subianto's announcement Monday signaled cautious optimism, with the Jakarta Composite Index erasing most of its session losses to end the day 0.1% lower.

Whether sentiment firms will depend on whether the new finance minister can communicate more convincingly than his predecessor, Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa, who was in the role for about a year.

Purbaya's tenure was marked by conflicting messages on fiscal policy, crucially over the commitment to keep the budget deficit under 3.0% of gross domestic product, said Capital Economics' Gareth Leather.

Suahasil will need to be much clearer about his priorities and provide investors with more consistent signals on fiscal policy, Leather said.

Execution will be key too.

OCBC thinks respecting the 3.0% limit seems manageable as the deficit is tracking at about 2.7% of GDP.

Still, Suahasil has his work cut out for him in navigating cash-intensive government programs and new policies including an initiative to manage commodity exports.

Economists at Citi don't expect to see a change in the political directions of flagship programs such as free meals and infrastructure. But management could change.

Suahasil, who has a doctorate from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, has been consistent in his priorities: quality of spending over headline expansion, tax administration over rate increases, and adherence to the deficit ceiling, Citi said.

"We expect tighter control of social spending leakage and greater use of state financial institutions to mobilize private capital for infrastructure, rather than balance-sheet expansion at the center," Citi's Ferry Wong said.

Stock-exchange reforms to address concerns brought up by index providers have been taken as a positive step toward a market turnaround. A similar investor-friendly pivot at the finance ministry could be the next trigger for putting Indonesia back in investors' good books.

data.title: REG - Proteome Sciences - Further GCLP Chemoproteomics contract secured
data.description:
RNS Number : 8217U Proteome Sciences PLC 15 September 2026  

15 September 2026

The information contained within this announcement is deemed by the Company to constitute inside information as stipulated under the UK Market Abuse Regulation

Proteome Sciences plc

(“Proteome Sciences” or the “Company”)

Further GCLP Chemoproteomics contract secured

As initially announced in June this year, Proteome Sciences plc (AIM:PRM) is pleased to now confirm that the Company has secured the expected significant clinical contract for its chemoproteomics platform.  This project has been developed to comply with Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (“GCLP”) accreditation and will be undertaken at our laboratories in Frankfurt, Germany.

This will be the 3rd contract connected with the same protein for both phase 1 and phase 2 clinical trials that are on-going globally.  Samples are expected to start to be shipped later this year.   The Company envisages that the majority of the work should be completed in 2027.

Richard Dennis, Chief Commercial Officer commented:-

“As reported previously, we continue to see demand from major biopharma clients in the US and Europe for GCLP grade protein assays that require the precision of sophisticated mass spectrometry-based techniques to provide the necessary data to demonstrate the effectiveness of drugs used in clinical trials today.  We anticipate increased requirement for this approach as more complex drugs are taken into clinical trials and future biomanufacturing”.

Proteome Sciences plc

About Proteome Sciences plc. (www.proteomics.com)

Proteome Sciences plc is a specialist provider of contract proteomics services to enable drug discovery, development and biomarker identification, and employs proprietary workflows for the optimum analysis of tissues, cells and body fluids. SysQuant® and TMT®MS2 are unbiased methods for identifying and contextualising new targets and defining mechanisms of biological activity, with analysis using a range of depletion strategies in combination with TMTcalibrator™ providing access to over 8,500 circulating plasma proteins for the discovery of disease-related biomarkers. Chemoproteomics using Solvent Shift  reveals the selectivity that drugs have to binding one or more proteins in the sample proteome.  Targeted assay development using mass spectrometry delivers high sensitivity, interference-free biomarker analyses in situations where standard ELISA assays are not available.

data.title: U.S. 10-Year Treasury Yield Rises to Highest Since 2007
data.description:
By Emese Bartha

The selloff in global bonds gained traction on Tuesday, pushing the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield to its highest level since 2007 after it rose above 5% for the first time in almost three years on Monday.

The 10-year Treasury yield hit a high of 5.041%, Tradeweb data showed, as heightened tensions in the Middle East fueled concerns over energy prices and inflation, leaving a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike on Wednesday looking close to certain.

"Rates markets remain hostage to oil and geopolitics ahead of Wednesday's Federal Open Market Committee [meeting]," Evelyne Gomez-Liechti, multiasset strategist at Mizuho said in a note.

Any brief optimism around Iran diplomacy on Monday proved short-lived and U.S. Treasurys were then sold as oil prices began to rise again.
